title: Let CLAUDE_CODE_CONTEXT_LIMIT set the context window for any model
description:
The resolver already reads CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS, but only honours it for models that pass an eligibility check — everything else falls through to the 200000 default. This adds an unconditional short-circuit at the top of the resolver, under a separate variable name so the official one keeps its meaning.

By 2.1.302 the resolver is split in two: a two-argument entry that answers the [1m] opt-in with 1e6 and clamps some models to 200000, wrapped around a one-argument body. Callers reach the body only through the entry, so the entry is where the short-circuit has to go; patching the body alone would leave the variable ignored for [1m] models and capped for the clamped ones. The body keeps its own short-circuit, as on an unsplit build, so a caller that ever reaches it directly is covered too.

sites.description: The resolver body: reads CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS, returns 1e6 early for the long-context cases, and ends at the default constant. The 1e6 return is the signal — of the functions mentioning the variable, no other returns it. Arity is not: this took (model, context) until the split and takes (model) after it.

The resolver's second parameter, the context it was handed. Present on an unsplit resolver; gone once it is the body of a split one, and then the split stage runs. Matched on the resolver itself so it hits on either shape — a probe that matched only the split shape would report drift on every unsplit build.

The entry in front of the split body: (model, context), returns 1e6 for the [1m] opt-in before it reaches the body, then calls the body and may clamp what it returns. Required once the split is seen — patching the body alone would leave both of those paths out.

verify.describe: resolver short-circuits on the env var
